title: Build a Mobile Manipulator: From Simulation to Real Hardware
summary: End-to-end robotics: design a mobile manipulator in simulation, implement perception + planning + control + manipulation, transfer to (real or HIL) hardware, and demonstrate a multi-step task.
contentIntro:
## What you'll build

A complete mobile manipulator system: a wheeled or legged base + a robot arm, navigating an environment + manipulating objects on command.

In simulation: full system from URDF to executing tasks. On real hardware (or hardware-in-the-loop simulation if hardware isn't available): the same stack with real sensor noise + real dynamics.

This capstone is the synthesis of the entire roboticist path. It exercises perception, estimation, planning, control, manipulation, sim-to-real, and learning-based components.

## What you'll demonstrate

- You can design + simulate a complete robot system.
- You can implement classical perception + estimation (SLAM, Kalman filtering).
- You can implement classical planning + control (motion planning, MPC, IK).
- You can integrate ML components (object detection, grasp prediction, behavior cloning).
- You can debug + tune real-world (or HIL) deployments.
- You can produce a clear writeup explaining design choices + lessons learned.
contentUndergrad:
## Why this capstone

Most robotics learning is fragmented: a SLAM tutorial, a motion-planning notebook, an IK exercise. Real robots are systems where these components interact + sometimes conflict. This capstone forces you to integrate them.

By the end you have one full mobile-manipulator artifact: working code, simulation videos, real (or HIL) hardware demos, and a defended report. Portfolio-worthy.

## Hardware options

**Option A: real hardware**. If you have access to a TurtleBot, JetBot, KUKA arm, Franka Panda, or similar — use it. The capstone milestones include hardware-specific calibration + deployment.

**Option B: hardware-in-the-loop simulation**. Use Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MuJoCo, or PyBullet to simulate the robot. Add domain randomization + noise to mimic hardware. Cheaper + accessible.

**Option C: pure simulation**. If hardware + HIL aren't feasible, build everything in simulation with realistic noise + dynamics. Less authentic but still valuable.

## Pacing

10 weeks at ~5-8 hrs/week. Most time: milestones 3 (SLAM + estimation), 5 (manipulation), 7 (integration + deployment). Milestones 1-2 are setup; 4 + 6 are mid-complexity.

## Tools

- **ROS 2** (preferred) or ROS 1 for system architecture.
- **Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MuJoCo, or PyBullet** for simulation.
- **OpenCV, PyTorch** for perception + ML.
- **GTSAM, Cartographer, ORB-SLAM3** for SLAM.
- **MoveIt!, OMPL** for motion planning + IK.
- **Drake, Pinocchio** for advanced control + dynamics.
- **Python + C++** for implementation.
contentGrad:
## Notes for the experienced

If you've worked in robotics professionally, the value of this capstone is the **integrated system view**. Most production roboticists are deep in one component (perception, planning, controls); this exercises all of them.

Likely places where production practitioners cut corners:

- Skipping rigorous SLAM accuracy testing.
- Using black-box IK without understanding singularities.
- Treating motion planning as solved (the first feasible path is rarely the best).
- Insufficient sim-to-real protocol.
- Missing failure-mode analysis.

The rubric specifically rewards rigor at the system level: how do components interact, where do failures compound, what testing approach catches problems.

## Variants

- **Manipulator-only variant**: drop the mobile base; focus on a fixed-base robot arm. Capstone timeline reduces to 7-8 weeks.
- **Mobile-only variant**: drop the manipulator; focus on autonomous navigation. Capstone timeline reduces to 7-8 weeks.
- **Learning-heavy variant**: replace classical components with learned policies (BC + diffusion + RL). Higher risk + reward.
- **Multi-robot variant**: two or more robots cooperating. Adds significant scope.

Author approval required for variants.

milestones.title: Robot design + simulation setup
milestones.description:
Design the robot. Specify: base type (wheeled / legged / static), arm type (DOF, payload), sensors (cameras, LIDAR, IMU). Build URDF (or MJCF for MuJoCo). Set up simulation environment with realistic physics + sensors.

**Deliverables**: URDF / MJCF file + a `setup.md` writeup justifying design choices + a video demonstrating the simulated robot moving in its environment.

milestones.title: Low-level control + IK
milestones.description:
Implement low-level joint controllers (PID or computed-torque). Implement forward + inverse kinematics. Verify by commanding the end-effector to a series of poses; record tracking error.

**Deliverables**: code (either in ROS controllers or Python) + a `control.md` writeup + plots of tracking error.

milestones.title: SLAM + state estimation
milestones.description:
Implement SLAM for the robot. Use either an existing system (Cartographer, ORB-SLAM3, GTSAM-based) or your own. Test in the simulated environment. Report mapping accuracy + localization drift.

**Deliverables**: SLAM implementation + a `slam.md` writeup + a video showing the robot mapping its environment + a quantitative accuracy report (e.g., trajectory error vs ground truth).

milestones.title: Motion planning + navigation
milestones.description:
Implement motion planning. For navigation: A* or RRT* on the SLAM map. For arm: RRT-Connect or trajectory optimization. Test multiple navigation goals + arm-reach goals in the simulated environment.

**Deliverables**: motion planner code + a `planning.md` writeup + videos showing successful navigation + arm motion through cluttered environments.

milestones.title: Perception + grasp planning
milestones.description:
Implement object detection + grasp prediction. Use either ML-based (Dex-Net-style or 6-DoF GraspNet) or classical (model-based grasp synthesis). Test on multiple objects + scenes.

**Deliverables**: perception + grasp code + a `perception.md` writeup + videos of detection + grasping + a quantitative success rate over diverse objects.

milestones.title: Sim-to-real protocol (or HIL transfer)
milestones.description:
If using real hardware: implement domain randomization + system identification; transfer the simulation-trained policies to hardware; report the gap.

If using HIL: add realistic sensor + dynamics noise to the simulation; transfer policies trained on the clean simulator to the noisy one; report the gap.

**Deliverables**: sim-to-real protocol code + a `sim2real.md` writeup + side-by-side comparison videos (sim vs hardware/HIL) + quantitative gap analysis.

milestones.title: End-to-end task + final demo
milestones.description:
Integrate all components: navigation + perception + manipulation. Demonstrate a multi-step task (e.g., 'go to the table, find the red block, pick it up, deliver to the kitchen, place it'). Record success rate over multiple trials.

**Deliverables**: integrated system code + a final `demo.md` writeup + a polished video of the end-to-end task + a success-rate report (at least 10 trials with documented outcomes).
